title: Bài 1: Sống Như Khách Lạ Trên Đất
subtitle: Living as Exiles — 1 Peter 1:3-7; 1 Peter 2:9-12 · Ngữ pháp: Perfect continuous tenses: present perfect continuous (have/has been + verb-ing) and past perfect continuous (had been + verb-ing)
grammar_topic: Perfect continuous tenses: present perfect continuous (have/has been + verb-ing) and past perfect continuous (had been + verb-ing)
pronunciation: Stress shift in word families: how stress moves when a suffix is added, and noun-verb stress pairs
pronunciation_detail:
Rule 1 — suffixes move the stress. When you add a suffix such as -graphy, -itance or -ation, the main stress usually moves to the syllable just before the suffix. PHOtograph becomes phoTOgraphy. INherit becomes inHERitance. IMmigrant becomes immiGRAtion. Learn the whole word family together, not one word alone.

Rule 2 — noun and verb pairs. Many two-syllable words change their stress when they change their job. As a noun, the stress falls on the first syllable; as a verb, it falls on the second. CONduct is a noun (your conduct = your behaviour), conDUCT is a verb (to conduct a meeting). PREsent is a noun (a gift), preSENT is a verb (to present a report). REcord is a noun, reCORD is a verb. OBject is a noun (a thing), obJECT is a verb (to disagree).

Rule 3 — the vowel changes with the stress. An unstressed vowel is usually reduced to a short, weak sound. In PHOtograph the first vowel is full, but in phoTOgraphy the first vowel is weak. Do not pronounce every syllable with full strength: English rhythm is strong-weak, strong-weak.

Practice. Say each pair aloud, clapping on the stressed syllable: PHOtograph, phoTOgraphy; INherit, inHERitance; IMmigrant, immiGRAtion; CONduct (noun), conDUCT (verb); PREsent (noun), preSENT (verb); REcord (noun), reCORD (verb). Then read 1 Peter 2:12 aloud and stress the noun CONduct correctly: Keep your CONduct among the Gentiles honorable.

Listen and repeat: PHOtograph — phoTOgraphy; INherit — inHERitance; IMmigrant — immiGRAtion; CONduct (noun: behaviour) — conDUCT (verb: to lead); PREsent (noun: a gift) — preSENT (verb: to give); REcord (noun: a written account) — reCORD (verb: to write down); OBject (noun: a thing) — obJECT (verb: to disagree); PROduce (noun: farm products) — proDUCE (verb: to make)
objectives: Hiểu và dùng thì hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn và quá khứ hoàn thành tiếp diễn (for / since; before / by the time; động từ trạng thái không dùng ở dạng tiếp diễn).
Phát âm: phân biệt trọng âm đổi chỗ trong họ từ (photograph / photography, inherit / inheritance) và cặp danh từ / động từ (conduct, present, record).
Đọc và hiểu 1 Phi-e-rơ 1:3–7 và 2:9–12 (ESV): hy vọng sống, cơ nghiệp không hư nát, dân được chọn, khách lạ và người tạm trú.
Nghe và trả lời 6 câu hỏi về thư của Phi-e-rơ gửi các tín hữu xa xứ.

grammar.title: Perfect continuous tenses: present perfect continuous (have/has been + verb-ing) and past perfect continuous (had been + verb-ing)
grammar.explain:
Form. Present perfect continuous: have / has + been + verb-ing. Past perfect continuous: had + been + verb-ing. Example: I have been living here for five years. They had been waiting for the Messiah for many years before Jesus came.

Use 1 — an action that started in the past and is still going on. Present perfect continuous stresses the activity and its duration, not the finished result. Use it with for (a length of time) and since (a starting point). Example: She has been studying English since 2020. We have been praying for our city all year.

Use 2 — a recent activity with a visible result now. Example: I have been reading First Peter this week, so my Bible is full of notes. Your eyes are red — have you been crying? The continuous form explains the present situation.

Present perfect continuous or present perfect simple? Use the continuous when you want to stress how long the activity has lasted. Use the simple when you want to stress the completed result or the number of times. Compare: I have been writing letters all morning (the activity lasted all morning) with I have written three letters this morning (the finished result: three letters).

Use 3 — past perfect continuous: a longer action that was in progress before another past event. The longer action uses had been + verb-ing; the shorter, later event uses the past simple. Example: The fishermen had been working all night before Jesus came to them. The believers had been praying together when the Spirit came.

Watch out — stative verbs. Verbs that describe a state, not an action, are not used in continuous forms: know, believe, belong, love, hate, understand, need, want. Say I have known him for years, not I have been knowing him for years. Say We have belonged to this church since 2019, not We have been belonging.

Common mistake. Do not use the present continuous for a long duration that reaches the present. Wrong: I am living here for five years. Right: I have been living here for five years. The present continuous (I am living here now) describes only this moment; the perfect continuous connects the past to the present.
examples: I have been living in Hanoi for five years.
She has been studying English since 2020.
They have been waiting for the bus for an hour.
We have been praying for our city all year.
I have been reading First Peter this week.
The fishermen had been working all night before Jesus came to them.
The believers had been praying together when the Spirit came.
He had been walking to the temple every day before he met Philip.

reading_passage: Peter wrote his first letter to Christians who were scattered across Asia Minor, far from Jerusalem and far from home. They were strangers in the cities where they lived. They had no power, no protection, and no permanent place. Some of them were suffering because of their faith. Peter did not tell them to fight for a home on earth. Instead, he told them about a better home. God, in his great mercy, had caused them to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead. Their inheritance was imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, kept in heaven for them. No thief could steal it, no fire could burn it, and no time could make it fade. While they waited, God himself was guarding them by his power through faith. Their trials were real, and Peter did not pretend otherwise. He said their faith was being tested like gold in fire, and tested faith is more precious than gold. Peter also told them who they were: a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God's own possession. God had called them out of darkness into his marvelous light so that they would proclaim his excellencies. And because they belonged to God, they were to live differently. As sojourners and exiles, they were to abstain from the passions of the flesh, which wage war against the soul, and to keep their conduct honorable among unbelievers, so that others would see their good deeds and glorify God. Peter's message is our message too. We are living far from our true home, but we are not homeless. Our inheritance is waiting, and our hope is alive.

reading_comprehension.q: 1. To whom did Peter write, and where were they living?
reading_comprehension.a: To Christians scattered across Asia Minor, living far from home as strangers in the cities where they lived.

reading_comprehension.q: 2. What three words describe the believers' inheritance in 1 Peter 1:4?
3. Who guards the believers while they wait, and how?
reading_comprehension.a: God guards them by his power through faith (1 Peter 1:5).

reading_comprehension.q: 4. What four things does Peter call believers in 1 Peter 2:9?
reading_comprehension.a: A chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, and a people for God's own possession.

reading_comprehension.q: 5. Why must believers keep their conduct honorable among unbelievers?
reading_comprehension.a: So that when others speak against them as evildoers, they may see their good deeds and glorify God on the day of visitation (1 Peter 2:12).

listening_questions.q: 1. Who wrote the letter the Narrator talks about, and to whom?
listening_questions.a: The apostle Peter, to Christians living far from home in places all over Asia Minor.

listening_questions.q: 2. What three words does Peter use to describe our inheritance?
3. What does 'sojourner' mean, according to the Narrator?
listening_questions.a: A person who is living for a time in a place that is not home.

listening_questions.q: 4. How long has the Friend been living in her city, and what has she been doing?
listening_questions.a: For five years; she has been learning the language and making friends.

listening_questions.q: 5. What had the first Christians been waiting for, before Jesus came?
6. What does Peter ask believers to do in 1 Peter 2:11-12?
listening_questions.a: To abstain from the passions of the flesh, which wage war against the soul, and to keep their conduct honorable, so that others may see their good deeds and glorify God.

exercises.title: Exercise 1: Stress Shift — Mark the Stressed Syllable
exercises.instruction: Mark the stressed syllable in each word of the pair. Remember: suffixes often move the stress to the syllable before the suffix, and noun-verb pairs stress the first syllable as a noun and the second as a verb.

exercises.title: Exercise 2: Present Perfect Continuous — have / has been + verb-ing
exercises.instruction: Complete each sentence with the present perfect continuous form of the verb in brackets. Use for or since where given.

exercises.title: Exercise 3: Past Perfect Continuous vs Past Simple
exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form. Past perfect continuous (had been + verb-ing) describes the longer action in progress before a past event; the shorter, later event uses the past simple.

exercises.title: Exercise 4: Vocabulary Matching
exercises.instruction: Match each word with its correct definition.

exercises.title: Exercise 5: Listening Comprehension
exercises.instruction: Listen to the audio (b2-lesson-01-listening.mp3) twice. Then answer the questions.

exercises.title: Exercise 6: Ministry Translation Lab (Vietnamese to English)
exercises.instruction: Translate into natural English. Use the perfect continuous tenses and this lesson's vocabulary.

speaking_task: Roleplay in pairs (3 minutes): Student A tells Student B about a time when you felt like a stranger in a new place (a new city, a new school, a new country). Student B asks two questions about it. Use at least 4 perfect continuous sentences (I have been living... / We had been waiting...) and 5 vocabulary words from Section 3. Practise the stress-shift pairs: photograph / photography, inherit / inheritance, CONduct (noun) / conDUCT (verb).
writing_task: Write a short essay (120-150 words) titled 'My Life as a Sojourner'. Describe where you live now, how long you have been living there, what you have been learning, and what hope you hold for the future. Use at least 4 perfect continuous sentences (present perfect continuous and past perfect continuous) and 5 vocabulary words from Section 3.

written: A. Write 5 sentences about your own life: 2 in the present perfect continuous (1 with for, 1 with since), 2 in the past perfect continuous, and 1 sentence that contrasts the present perfect simple with the present perfect continuous.
B. Write 1 Peter 2:11 in English from memory, then check your work against the Bible.
homework.listening: Listen to the audio again. Fill in the missing words: 'Their inheritance was ______, ______, and ______, kept in heaven for them.' Then answer: What does the Friend say she has been doing for five years?
